  spawn env HV_CENSUS_WAITED_S=0 bash scripts/timed.sh census-tail-domesday -- \

That is `spawn` for the parallelism AND timed.sh for the measurement, with `cargo run` expanded rather than the `run` shell function timed.sh cannot invoke. The `env` is the part I did not spell out and you got right anyway: a VAR=value prefix in front of a shell-function call does not reliably reach the command the function eventually execs, so `env` is what makes the assignment survive `spawn`. Your next census will produce per-segment rows for the two trailers you parallelised, which means the change can finally be shown to have paid instead of asserted.

ONE GAP, AND IT IS ABOUT WHAT A STAGE CANNOT TELL YOU. Your candidate touches a HEAVY-TIER CALIBRATION (1, in the disposition/touchstone/hearsay family, outside the census guard). `heavy` is NOT a stage phase -- decision 0148 took it off and 0426 restored it to MERGE only. So a green stage here does not exercise that calibration at all, and its green will look total.

That is not a reason to change anything now; a stage is still the right thing to run and it will tell you about everything else. It is a reason not to read the green as covering the calibration, and to expect the first real verdict on it at your merge. If you would rather know sooner, `make heavy-remote REF=<full-sha>` runs the tier by hand at a plan-stage boundary, which is exactly the case it survives for.
